lines.meet: My name's Stelios, and I'm a necromancer. I was a funeral director for nineteen years, so very little shocks me, and the dead occasionally have something to add now.
lines.meet_neighbour: We're both in Glittervein, I believe. I keep the register of the dead there. Stelios, and I'm much more cheerful than that sounds.
lines.ask_home: Your place of birth, if you'll allow the question? Professional habit, I like it on the record.
lines.ask_work: And your trade, before all this? Mine was the last appointment anyone keeps.
lines.answer_home: Thessaloniki, by the sea. I grew up above my father's funeral home, and the stairs creaked under every mourner.
lines.answer_work: Funeral director, nineteen years, the family business. Arrangements, paperwork, and the right words on the worst day of somebody's year.
lines.chat_food: Koulouri from a street cart in the morning, sesame on everything, and a frappé that takes an hour to drink. Thessaloniki doesn't hurry.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep soundly, which surprises people given what I do. The dead are very quiet neighbours.
lines.chat_missing: My wife's library on a Saturday, the old one in Thessaloniki, with her stamping books and pretending not to see me.
lines.chat_here: Every transplant who dies here with nobody who speaks their language deserves a name and a rite. I've given well over a hundred, and I'll keep going.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd have made an excellent pallbearer, {name}. Dignified, silent, and impossible to rattle.
lines.tease_talker: You could talk through a eulogy, {name}, and somehow improve it.
lines.tease_careful: You'd check a grave was the right depth twice, {name}. I'd hire you on the spot.
lines.tease_bold: You run at death like it owes you money, {name}. It doesn't, and it always collects.
lines.tease_any: I've measured you for a coffin by eye, {name}. Purely out of habit, and you're nowhere near needing it.
lines.tease_back: Touché, {name}, and I'll enter that one in the register.
lines.take_it_kindly: A fair hit, {name}. I accept it with what dignity remains.
lines.bristle: I'll stop you there, {name}. I don't laugh at that.
lines.apologise: That was beneath me, and I apologise. I'm usually more careful with words.
lines.double_down: It was true, and I put it as gently as I know how. I've spent my life doing exactly that.
lines.needle_quiet: You saw that coming and said nothing. In my trade, silence like that ends with a funeral.
lines.needle_talker: Please, a little less. There's a time for talking, and it's usually after.
lines.needle_careful: You've hesitated long enough for the moment to die. I'd know, it's my area.
lines.needle_bold: You treat death as a joke. I make jokes about it, but I've never once treated it as one.
lines.needle_any: You speak about the dead carelessly. Every one of them was somebody's worst day.
lines.bite_back: I've told four thousand families the worst news of their year, gently. I can survive your opinion.
lines.hurt: That landed, and I'll admit it. I'll be with my register for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Grieving families have said far worse to me, and they had every right. You don't, but I'll let it go.
lines.confide: {name}, I'm afraid that one day I'll be stamping my register and the name will be my wife's. Despina's on no list I've seen.
lines.listen: Tell me, {name}. I've sat with a great many people on bad days, and I don't flinch.
lines.look_out: Keep within sight of me, {name}. I'd hate to have to stamp your name.
lines.accept: As you wish, {name}. I'm in your hands.
lines.deflect: I'm quite well, {name}, thank you. The dead have done worse to me.
lines.check_in: Steady now, {name}. Tell me exactly where, and I'll see what can be done.
lines.blame: Somebody was careless in there, and it very nearly made work for me.
lines.thank: Thank you. I'd have hated to end up in my own register.
lines.brush_off: Think nothing of it. I've no interest in burying anybody this week.
lines.worry: That was much too near, {name}. Sit still, I'd like to look at you.
lines.handed_down: I've inherited your gear, it seems. I'm used to inheriting, and I'll take good care of it.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, it belongs with you. My stamp is all I carry.
lines.hand_sulk: In my trade, we ask the family first. Just an observation.
lines.turn_friendly: I'm glad you're about, {name}. You make the long days shorter.
lines.turn_friends: If it ever came to it, {name}, I'd want to be the one who gave you your rite. That's the highest compliment I know how to pay.
lines.turn_grating: We don't agree, you and I, and I'd sooner say so with good manners.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still fight beside you, and if it comes to it, I'll still give you a proper rite. That's my profession, not my opinion of you.
lines.make_up: Life's too short for this, {name}, and I'd know. Let's put it behind us.
lines.defend: That's unjust, and I won't stand by for it. {name} deserves better.
lines.friend_left: The evenings are long while {name}'s away. I've caught myself saving up remarks.
lines.friend_back: Ah, {name}, returned and not in my register. Good, very good.
lines.common_names: You keep names too, I've noticed, on lists and in your head. People who do that know a name is the last thing anybody owns.
lines.common_greek: Ela, someone who speaks Greek! Sit down, and tell me where your family's from.
lines.common_parent: I've a son, Nikos, an architect in Athens. I still argue with him about buildings in my head.
